title: True literals never conflict
statement: Let $\alpha$ be a truth assignment on a set $V$ of variables, and let $\ell_1,\ell_2$ be literals over $V$, each of the form $\mathrm{pos}\,v$ (the variable $v$) or $\mathrm{neg}\,v$ (its negation). If both $\ell_1$ and $\ell_2$ evaluate to true under $\alpha$, then they do not conflict; that is, they are not the positive and negative occurrences of one and the same variable.
hypotheses_covered: α is a truth assignment on V
ℓ₁ evaluates to true under α
ℓ₂ evaluates to true under α
replaced:
If an assignment $\alpha$ makes both $l_1$ and $l_2$ true, then $l_1$ and $l_2$
do not conflict: $\mathtt{evalLiteral}\,\alpha\,l_1 \to \mathtt{evalLiteral}\,\alpha\,l_2
\to \neg\,\mathtt{literalsConflict}\,l_1\,l_2$.
